label: verify-pp-clients-and-contracts

claims.claim: SBIR/STTR is reauthorized through 30 Sep 2031 and ceilings are Phase I $335,937 / Phase II $2,239,578.
claims.source_says: Crowell: "through September 30, 2031", signed April 13, 2026. sbir.gov: As of October 16, 2026, Phase I "up to $335,937", Phase II "up to $2,239,578" without SBA approval.
claims.note: Both pages give the dates and figures stated.

claims.claim: Small businesses may keep title to federally funded inventions; government gets a paid-up licence.
claims.source_says: A small business firm "may, within a reasonable time after disclosure" elect to retain title; the agency gets a "nonexclusive, nontransferrable, irrevocable, paid-up license" (202(a), (c)(4)).
claims.note: Matches 35 USC 202, with the election made within a reasonable time after disclosure.

claims.claim: University sponsored research agreements generally offer a sponsor an option to negotiate a licence, not an outright licence.
claims.source_says: "We may only offer an option to negotiate a license or a right of first refusal to negotiate a license."
claims.note: The source is one university system's checklist, so it says what UT System does, not what universities do in general.

claims.claim: Lean 4, mathlib4 and Apache-2.0 library code allow commercial redistribution with notice and licence-copy conditions and a patent-litigation termination clause.
claims.source_says: Section 2: "perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright license" incl. sublicense and distribute; 4(a) "must give ... a copy of this License"; patent licences "shall terminate" on litigation.
claims.note: The mathlib4 LICENSE page was read and is Apache 2.0. The Lean 4 page fetch returned Apache 2.0 text. The Apache terms are as stated.

overall: All four key claims hold against the sources. The university claim is partly supported only because it generalises from one system (UT) to all universities.
